newsitem.title: USA: Sara Lee profits jump 10.8 percent.
newsitem.headline: Sara Lee profits jump 10.8 percent.

text.p: Sara Lee Corp. Wednesday reported a 10.8 percent jump in profits for the latest quarter and said it was on its way to post record results for the year.

The consumer products company said it earned $206 million, or 41 cents a share, in its fiscal first quarter vs. year-ago earnings of $186 million, or 37 cents a share. Sales rose to $4.9 billion from $4.7 billion.

"A combination of internal growth and acquisitions contributed to our sales and operating profit gains during the quarter," said Chairman John Bryan. "We expected continued record sales and earnings throughout the remainder of fiscal 1997."

Over the years, Sara Lee has soared as a consumer products company through its acquisitions of companies such as food maker Hillshire Farm and Jimmy Dean, intimate apparel manufacturer Hanes and the hosiery firm L'eggs.
The company said its packaged meats and bakery unit had a strong quarter, with profits jumping 19.2 percent and sales gaining 17.0 percent, boosted by the acquisition of Aoste, a European meats firm.

It said sales at the coffee and grocery division were off 7.1 percent, partly due to a stronger dollar relative to European currencies, and personal products sales edged up 0.5 percent from a year ago.
Sara Lee's stock was unchanged at $36.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
